title: ADR Decision Record v1
description: One record per architecture decision, appended once to specs/ADRs/decisions.jsonl (v0.5.0 specs-canon closure, operator ruling 2026-08-28). A superseded decision stays in decisions.jsonl with `status: superseded`, named by its successor's `supersedes`; its id is never reused (0.4.7 FR8 retired the `_superseded/` lane — a second file the record had to be MOVED to, which shipped empty and split one inventory in two). `id` is monotonic and gap-free over the one file. Any agent may append a `status: proposed` record; ONLY the operator flips `status` to `accepted` (specs/ADRs/AGENTS.md's operator-only acceptance law) — `accepted` requires a RESOLVABLE `measured_by` (a decision nobody can run is not a principle, it is prose).

id.description: Zero-padded 4-digit sequence number, monotonic and gap-free over decisions.jsonl — never reused, never re-numbered.

ts.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp this record was appended.

status.description: proposed: any agent may author, EXCEPT a record born from an operator grill ruling, which is appended `accepted` with the ruling date in `context`. accepted: operator-only, requires a resolvable measured_by. rejected: operator decision, no consequence elsewhere. superseded: retired in place by the successor named in that successor's `supersedes`.

context.description: What forces make this decision necessary — the problem, not the solution.

decision.description: "We will …" — the choice, stated as a commitment, not a discussion.

measured_by.description: The existing mechanical check that proves this decision holds. Free text while `proposed`; once `accepted` it must match the resolvable pattern in this schema's allOf — a pytest invocation, a lint-imports invocation, or a code a reader greps for (SPEC-DOC-nnn, WS-*, BL-*, RELEASE-TREE-*, LEDGER-*), or `dadaia doctor`/`dadaia bugs status`.

supersedes.description: Id (NNNN) of the record this one supersedes, or null.

amends.description: Id (NNNN) of the record this one amends, or null.

allOf.description: The operator-only acceptance law, expressed MECHANICALLY (0.4.7 FR6): an 'accepted' record must carry a non-empty 'measured_by' — a decision nobody can measure is not a principle, it is prose. Stated in this schema rather than in a test's hand-rolled copy, so the one validator the ledgers doctor runs and the one the contract test runs are the same validator. 0.4.7 FR8 tightened non-empty to RESOLVABLE: five of the ten committed records were accepted naming the sentence 'specs doctor release rules + dd-gitflow-default conformance in audits', which resolved to nothing runnable — minLength alone cannot tell a check from a wish.

examples.title: Features depend on ports, not adapters
examples.context: Features need I/O (git, filesystem, subprocess) but must stay unit-testable without real I/O.
examples.decision: We will define a Protocol in core/protocols/ for every I/O boundary a feature needs, and inject a concrete infrastructure/ adapter at the composition root (container.py) — a feature module never imports infrastructure directly.
examples.consequences:
+ features are testable with fakes, no real I/O in unit tests
- one extra indirection layer per I/O boundary
